provenance: Lane split authored by the Stage-2 decision-agent (read-only; returns JSON in reply) and persisted by the orchestrator as the agent's returned detect-vs-hunt partition. Detection = seed complement of the agent's hunt set; validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup, and det-count reconciled against the agent's summary. All ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset. Per-technique rationale shows the Stage-1 detection-feasibility basis.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — provider-originated access is detectable via anomalous third-party/remote-management logons and unexpected provider account activity, but requires baselining of legitimate provider behavior

medium — the delivery occurs on third-party sites (off-victim), but the resulting browser-to-payload chain and outbound requests to profiling/staging domains are detectable via proxy and browser child-process telemetry on the victim endpoint
medium — SQLi and web-app exploitation are detectable via WAF alerts, web-server error/anomaly logs and unexpected DB-to-shell process chains, but require web-tier instrumentation
medium — valid-account abuse is detectable via anomalous logon analytics (impossible travel, new host/time) but blends with legitimate use
medium — privileged domain-account use is detectable via anomalous admin-logon and privileged-group authentication analytics, but requires identity telemetry and good baselines
high — script-block/module logging and suspicious PowerShell parenting are core, well-covered detections

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: high — cmd.exe execution with anomalous parents and staged-binary paths (\Windows\Temp) is visible in process-creation logs

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
detection_candidates.rationale: high — wscript/cscript executing VBS, especially spawned by Office or archive extraction, is a strong detectable signal
medium — malicious-link clicks are detectable via URL-gateway/proxy logs; endpoint signal is indirect
high — user-launched installers/documents spawning script or child processes is a core detectable behavior
high — mshta.exe executing HTA/remote content and spawning child processes is a rare LOLBin pattern with low false-positive rate
high — WMI process creation and WMI-Activity operational logs provide strong telemetry
high — scheduled-task creation is logged (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational) and highly detectable, especially with script/binary actions

detection_candidates.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
detection_candidates.rationale: high — service creation (Event ID 7045 / 4697) and NSSM-registered services are strongly detectable

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: high — Run-key writes are logged via registry-modification telemetry and are a well-covered persistence detection

detection_candidates.technique_name: Hijack Execution Flow: DLL Search Order Hijacking
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — side-loading is detectable via unusual DLL loads from non-standard paths by signed binaries (image-load telemetry), but requires module-load logging and good baselines
medium — injection is detectable via EDR cross-process memory-write/thread-creation telemetry but generates volume that needs behavioral correlation
medium — in-memory .NET/reflective loading is detectable via CLR-load and AMSI/ETW telemetry but requires managed-runtime instrumentation
medium — obfuscation is inferable from static/entropy analysis but needs dedicated inspection

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — high-entropy/encoded payloads are detectable via file-entropy analytics but require dedicated scanning
high — 'certutil -decode' and in-script decode routines are directly observable in command-line and script-block logging
medium — masquerading is detectable via name/path baselining and signature/content mismatch analysis

detection_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — legit-looking names in non-standard/temp paths are detectable via path/name baselining and signature mismatch
medium — registry modification is logged, but volume is high; value comes from watching the specific policy keys the actor sets
medium — file deletion is detectable via file-system audit / EDR delete events but is noisy and needs correlation with prior payload writes
medium — signature-trust abuse is detectable via certificate/thumbprint and load-path anomaly analytics on loaded binaries
high — process access to lsass.exe and ProcDump/Mimikatz signatures are highly observable in EDR and process-access telemetry
medium — password-store access is detectable mainly through known-tool execution and file/DPAPI-access telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — access to browser Login Data stores is detectable via file-access and known-tool telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Windows Credential Manager
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — Credential Manager/vault access is detectable via known-tool signatures and DPAPI/file-access telemetry
medium — systeminfo discovery is common; suspicious mainly in tight process-lineage/recon-burst context
medium — 'ipconfig' is common but suspicious when clustered with other recon in a short process-lineage window
medium — whoami/logon-history enumeration is common; value is in process-lineage correlation and the distinctive get-logon-history.ps1 tool name
medium — process enumeration is common but meaningful in recon-burst/process-lineage context
high — 'net user'/'net localgroup' enumeration is directly observable in command-line logging
high — 'net user /domain' / 'net group /domain' enumeration is directly observable in command-line logging
high — 'net localgroup administrators' is directly observable in command-line logging
medium — security-software enumeration is detectable via command-line and process queries against AV services/registry, but is low-volume and needs targeted rules
medium — 'netstat' is common; meaningful in recon-burst/process-lineage context
medium — service enumeration is common; suspicious mainly in recon-burst/process-lineage context
medium — RDP lateral movement is detectable via 4624 type-10 logons and internal-RDP fanout analytics
high — PsExec/PAExec service creation over admin shares (7045, 5145, remote service install) is strongly detectable
medium — local collection is common; suspicious mainly via staging/archiving and upload command-lines in process-lineage context

detection_candidates.technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — archive-utility execution (rar/7z/zip) against staged data is detectable via process command-lines but needs correlation with prior collection
medium — HTTP C2 is detectable via proxy/beacon analytics and URI/JA3 anomalies but blends with normal web traffic
high — remote downloads via certutil/PowerShell and unexpected inbound file writes are strongly detectable in process + network telemetry
medium — base64-encoded C2 content is detectable via network inspection/encoding heuristics where TLS is absent
medium — C2-channel exfil is detectable via outbound-volume anomalies on beaconing sessions, though the mail-based variant blends into normal mail flow

low — client-side software enumeration is not visible in victim server/endpoint logs; hunt candidate only
low — off-victim infrastructure acquisition is not endpoint-observable; intel/hunt candidate via lookalike-domain and registration monitoring
low — off-victim web-service acquisition; intel/hunt candidate
low — persona account creation is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via persona and social-graph analysis
low — social-media persona creation is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate
low — off-victim mailbox creation; intel/hunt candidate (downstream IMAP C2 use is where detection lands, see T1071.003)
low — capability development is not observable in victim telemetry; intel/hunt candidate
low — tool acquisition is off-endpoint; downstream use is detectable — this entry is a hunt/intel candidate
low — staging on adversary infrastructure is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via lookalike-site and hosting monitoring
low — drive-by staging occurs on third-party sites; intel/hunt candidate via third-party web-content integrity monitoring
low — upstream supply-chain compromise is largely outside a downstream victim's endpoint visibility; strategic intel/hunt candidate

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — software supply-chain compromise is upstream and hard to see from the victim; hunt candidate via unexpected provider-pushed binaries and integrity monitoring
low — social-media-delivered lures bypass corporate mail gateways; user-awareness/hunt candidate with limited endpoint signal
low — the JavaScript runs in visitors' browsers on third-party sites; limited victim-endpoint signal; hunt candidate via web-content integrity monitoring
low — keystroke-hooking APIs leave little discrete log signal; behavioral/EDR hunt candidate
low — credential harvesting occurs on attacker-hosted portals off the victim endpoint; hunt/intel candidate via phishing-page and domain monitoring
low — reading credential-bearing files leaves little discrete log signal; hunt candidate via file-access telemetry
low — file/directory enumeration is high-volume and low-signal; hunt candidate via behavioral correlation
low — screen-capture APIs leave little discrete log signal; behavioral/EDR hunt candidate
low — automated collection leaves little discrete log signal beyond the tool execution itself; behavioral/EDR hunt candidate
low — local staging in temp is common and noisy; better as a hunt over file-write telemetry to \Windows\Temp

low — IMAP/email-based C2 blends into normal mail traffic and its content is often encrypted; strong HUNT candidate via anomalous host-initiated IMAP to non-corporate mail providers, non-mail-client processes speaking IMAP, and beacon-like mailbox polling
low — symmetric-encrypted C2 content defeats content inspection; hunt on beacon/traffic-shape anomalies
low — proxy/relay use is inferred from network analysis; hunt candidate via connections to known-bad or anomalous intermediary infrastructure
low — browser-originated exfil to a web service from third-party sites is largely off victim-endpoint; hunt candidate via proxy telemetry to newly-registered profiling domains
